config.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair

personas.name: Odette
personas.goals: Keep the garden open and friendly
personas.hidden_agenda: Doesn't want a garden that feels like a fortress

personas.name: Ike
personas.role: Plot holder, upset about the thefts
personas.hidden_agenda: Lost his entire tomato crop and is furious

personas.name: Raul
personas.hidden_agenda: Installed the timers himself on a weekend

personas.name: Petra
personas.goals: A fair that funds the garden
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to sell plant starts from her own greenhouse

agenda.title: Produce theft
agenda.goal: Decide what to do about the thefts

agenda.title: Fees and hours
agenda.goal: Confirm next year's fee and volunteer hours

beats.summary: How bad it is; Ike exaggerates, then the options
Timers and the bill; Raul's figure stands
The spring fair; Petra's profit memory is high, corrected later; a detour about a neighbor's chickens

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Let's start with the thefts. I know people are upset.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Upset is an understatement. There have been over twenty thefts this season. My tomatoes are gone. All of them.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: I'm so sorry, Ike. The log has nine reports, though. Maybe some weren't reported?

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Nine reported. Probably more that people didn't bother to write down.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Mine weren't touched, for what it's worth. It seems to be the plots by the back gate.

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: The back gate is the one with the broken latch. Anyone can push it open.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Then why hasn't it been fixed?

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: I've fixed it twice. It keeps getting forced.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: We need a taller fence. Now.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: The fence quote was forty-two hundred. That's more than we have.

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: The balance is thirty-seven hundred. So, no fence this year.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: What about a trail camera? They're about three hundred and fifty.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: I don't love cameras in a community garden. It feels unfriendly.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: It feels unfriendly to have your tomatoes stolen.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Fair. Okay, a camera on the back gate only, and a sign saying it's there.

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: I'll buy the camera and put it up this weekend, and fix the latch properly with a padlock.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Do we change the gate code again? That's twice already this year.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Not yet. Let's see if the camera helps first.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Fine.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Water. Raul?

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: We have eight timers on the main beds now. The bill last season was twenty-two hundred, so they should help a lot.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: That's a lot of water for forty-four plots.

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: The timers alone should cut it by a quarter.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Do we need more timers?

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: Two more would cover the herb beds. They're cheap.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Then let's get two more.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: My plot's tap leaks, by the way. It'd be nice if it got looked at before summer.

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: Send me a photo and I'll fix it.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: The fair. It's on May tenth. Last year we made about three thousand.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: That would be lovely again.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Could we sell the excess produce at the fair? Well, what's left of it.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Absolutely. A produce table would be great.

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: The neighbor's chickens got into the garden again on Tuesday. They ate half my lettuce.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Maybe the chickens are the thieves.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: The chickens don't take whole tomatoes, Ike.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: The fair. Petra, tell us what you need.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Sorry, I just found last year's report. We made nineteen twenty, not three thousand. Three thousand was before the tent rental.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Nineteen twenty. Still very useful.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: I'd like to sell plant starts from my greenhouse at the fair, with the money going to the garden.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: That's generous. Yes, please.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: I'll make the posters and put them up at the library and the cafe.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Fees. The plot fee is fifty, and six volunteer hours per plot.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: If we need a fence, maybe the fee should go up.

turns.speaker: Raul
turns.text: Sixty dollars would raise four hundred and forty more. Not a fence, but a start.

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: Let's put the fee question to the members at the fair, so everyone has a say.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Who counts the votes at the fair?

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Do we know if the city has any grants for garden fencing?

turns.speaker: Odette
turns.text: I don't know. I'll look into it this week. Thank you, everyone.

turns.speaker: Petra
turns.text: Ike, I really am sorry about your tomatoes.

turns.speaker: Ike
turns.text: Thanks. Next year they'll be behind a camera.
